name: fragment-varying-float-to-half

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-fourteen-dual-output

name: kernel-stage-input-word

name: imageblock-word
rationale: One invocation initializes its explicit imageblock cell, reads it back, and writes 42 to a poisoned output buffer; 1x1 authored dimensions exercise the host allocation contract on Metal and the descriptor-free Workgroup lowering on Vulkan.

name: bicubic-at-four-texel-centres-of-three-array-slices
rationale:
Seventy-five corpus modules declare a bicubic sampler, and the lowering answers them with a hand-written sixteen-tap Catmull-Rom filter. Nothing had ever checked that against the hardware. The first question a bicubic emulation has to get right is which cubic family it is: an interpolating one returns the texel exactly at a texel centre, an approximating B-spline returns a blur of one sixth, two thirds, one sixth. This case asks the hardware that question.

The scale factor is one, so each of the four threads samples the centre of its own texel and both coordinate fractions are zero. The kernel loops over three array slices and writes the sampled red channel splatted across all four output channels, so the twelve observed halves are twelve source texels read back unchanged if and only if the filter interpolates. The source texels are sixty-fourths, which are exact halves, and each slice is offset so a slice mix-up is visible. The other three channels of each source texel hold different values so a channel swizzle is visible too.

Metal answers the texels exactly, so its filter::bicubic interpolates - the family the lowering picked. The companion case reads the weights themselves.

name: read-three-catmull-rom-weights-off-the-hardware-at-two-fractions
rationale:
The companion to the texel-centre bicubic case: this one reads Metal's cubic weights off the hardware one at a time instead of inferring the family.

Each source slice is zero everywhere except a single column of ones, and the column is constant down the whole height. A tap column that is constant in y makes the four y weights sum to exactly one, so the sampled value collapses to the single x weight at the tap that lands on the column - the shader reads out one filter coefficient as a number. The scale factor 5.5 puts the two threads at coordinate 2.25 and 7.75, so their fractions are a quarter and three quarters and their four-tap footprints, x=1..4 and x=6..9, do not overlap and do not reach an edge. The column position advances by one per array slice, so the three slices read the first three taps of each footprint.

Catmull-Rom with a = -1/2 predicts -9/128, 111/128 and 29/128 at a quarter and -3/128, 29/128 and 111/128 at three quarters. All six are exact halves, so the readout is byte-exact rather than approximate. Metal answers all six, which pins its filter::bicubic to the same cubic the lowering emits - including the negative lobes, which is what tells an interpolating cubic from a smoothing one.

name: extend-the-right-edge-of-a-three-tap-box-blur-past-the-destination-width
rationale:
A three-tap horizontal box blur over ARGB8 with edge-mode extend, 190 lines and one of 21 corpus hosts of `native/emitter/pointers/raw_select.rs::emit_raw_pointer_select_byte`, none of which had an authored case. The rule is the byte-granular twin of the word-granular pointer-select tail: thread zero picks the right-hand halo texel from either `&row[count]` or `&row[count - 1]` depending on whether the window runs past the source width, and both arms are raw byte offsets into the same device buffer, so the merged pointer is emitted as a select between two byte indices rather than between two pointers. The source is five pixels wide and the destination four, so `count + src_x_offset` is 4 and `src_width` is 5: the select takes its TRUE arm and reads pixel four, which no other output pixel reads and which differs from pixel three in three of its four channels. A select that picked the other arm would change the last destination pixel.

Every source channel is 0x00 or 0xFF, so every unpacked lane is exactly +0.0 or +1.0 and every window sums to 0, 1 or 2 -- exact in half and independent of the order the three addends are combined in, which is what makes the answer association-proof under `fast` math. The channel patterns are chosen so no window ever sums to 3, whose product with the literal 1/3 (`0xH3555`, 0.333251953125) lands exactly on a half rounding tie. The two products that do occur, 0.333251953125 and 0.66650390625, are exact halves and pack to 0x55 and 0xAA with no tie either. Every params byte outside the seven fields the kernel loads is 0xCC, including `background_color`, which this edge mode never reads. `loop_free`: the entry has no back edge.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-vector-matrix
rationale: One invocation uses a one-element linked destination array. The authored user constant selects eight-bit quantization, group size one, and zero vector rows; the exact zero K parameter makes both accumulation counts zero. Every arithmetic loop and the final postfix loop is therefore zero-trip, so the poisoned linked destination remains byte-exact while the wrapper and linkage contract execute.

name: merge-two-descriptors-at-a-phi-and-index-both-arms
rationale: A device pointer merged across TWO DESCRIPTORS by a phi, twice, with the two merges taking opposite arms. Logical SPIR-V has no value that can be either descriptor, so the translator lowers each merge to a PhysicalStorageBuffer64 device address: it synthesizes an address table, loads each buffer's address from it, phis between the two ADDRESSES, and turns every index off a merged pointer into a physical access chain. Coverage, measured rather than assumed: this is the SECOND case to reach construct_interface_cross_binding_pointer_phis_module, not the first -- irreducible-pointer-phi-rebuild-observed-at-arm-2 already does. Compared against it under llvm-cov, this module reaches no psb/pointer FUNCTION that case misses (it misses 18 that case reaches), and takes five branches inside psb_value_select's discover_value_selects, rewrite_cross_binding_pointer_merges_to_values and phi_suffix_indices_dominate_predecessors, plus one in Emitter::pointer_meta_for_value, that it does not. What it adds semantically is the shape that case has no room for: TWO merges over the SAME descriptor pair with opposite arms, and an index re-derived off one of them at a second dynamic offset. a holds 100+i and b holds 200+i, so the arm each merge chose is legible in the output word itself. p takes a on lanes 0-3 and b on lanes 4-7; q takes the other one; the third row reads p again at 7-gid, so a merge re-derived per use rather than carried has to agree with itself. All 24 expected words are distinct: out[0..7]=100 101 102 103 204 205 206 207, out[8..15]=200 201 202 203 104 105 106 107, out[16..23]=107 106 105 104 203 202 201 200. A swapped arm turns the first row into the second; a merge that collapses to one descriptor makes rows one and two equal; a leak between p and q swaps them on one half of the grid; and an index recomputed from the wrong merge puts b's words in the third row's low lanes. Every value is an exact small integer, so nothing here depends on rounding or on association.
